quest.title: Valor's Afterglow: Return by Sundown
quest.description: Jinwu has an urgent task for you. It seems to involve Zhiqiong...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Ugh, it's Zhiqiong again... She went to retrieve those beacons, and hasn't been back since.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: I gave her three extra hours, knowing that dumb habit she has of running around everywhere... But it's been at least five or six hours since.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Could you help me look for her? That kid really respects you, so you should have an easier time... and I don't want to have anyone get in trouble on my watch again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gah, what's with her, running off again like that?

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: Ah, yes! Silly me, I almost forgot to tell you the most important thing!

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: She probably didn't go too far, but at the same time, where would she go...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, don't worry about it, Jinwu! We'll head over to the places where we placed the beacons yesterday first!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's a pretty good call, Paimon.

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: Alright... alright then. If you find her, please inform me as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: How's Zhiqiong? Have you found her?

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: Alright, but please, find her soon. If something happens...

talks.objective: Go to the beacon placement sites to look for Zhiqiong
Go to the beacon placement sites to look for Zhiqiong

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you still walk?

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: Sorry... I'm sorry, Jinwu... and... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: Don't look at me... *cough* Don't look at me like that. Please, don't be disappointed in us... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: The golden city... The black watchtower...! *cough* The heavenly envoys have left...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cut it with the nonsense, you!

talks.objective: Go to the beacon placement sites to look for Zhiqiong
Go to the beacon placement sites to look for Zhiqiong

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Khedive's given her some medicine... and she's regained consciousness, but she won't tell me anything.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Do you know what happened? How did she end up like... that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She was trapped in the black mud when we found her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, and we got her out just in time!

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Never mind that for now. What Zhiqiong needs now is rest. Could you help me deliver this bowl of soup to her while it's still hot?

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: I'm not a very good cook, but I've had to take care of my fair share of miners, and no one's ever said my fare was bad.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Alright, go then. See if she's any better.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: I have to tell Muning that Zhiqiong can't stay underground anymore.

talks.objective: Go to the beacon placement sites to look for Zhiqiong

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: *cough* *cough* I'm sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're sorry now, and not when you were running around all over the place, huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright, give it a rest, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: *cough* Hah... I lost my footing... by mistake... funny, huh? *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, it's not funny at all! Is your life really worth so little to you!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You need rest. Jinwu made you some soup.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh! She's not looking so good! C'mon, we've got to get her out of here, quick!

choices.text: Don't worry, I'll take you back.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: Eh? Oh, my bad. There were some things on my mind. Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: I have to give Zhiqiong a good talking-to...

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: It's not like I haven't seen kids like her while working in the mines all these years...

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: There are too many who, like her, see adventure as some kind of noble pursuit, only to see their hopes shattered... and find that it is too late to regret their choices.

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: And yet, who am I to judge? *sigh* How could a Violetgrass lodged in a cliff's cleft criticize a bird for its way of life?

dialogues.speaker: Jinwu
dialogues.text: And yet, how can I just let it go like... *cough* You know what? Maybe stopping her is the wrong thing to do. I mean, she's an adult who can take care of herself already, isn't she?

response.speaker: Jinwu
response.text: I suppose... I hope you're right.

talks.objective: Talk to Zhiqiong, who has woken up

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: Jinwu made this...? Thank you... and please help me thank Jinwu and the others, too.

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: I'll be fine, I just need to get some sleep and I'll be good as new...

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: I'm really very sorry... *cough* Could you please come back again in a bit?

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: Hello there! Have a seat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about our previous adventure...

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: Ah, are you trying to ask why I was so stubborn or why I gave everyone so much trouble? Haha, come on, I know I was wrong... you don't have to keep harping on it...

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: But to be honest, I suspect that it's in our nature as adventurers to be fascinated with danger.

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: I mean, we were born with strong backs and agile limbs. It just feels... wrong, you know? To have these tools but be content with a placid existence.

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: As for mortal peril, it's not that I haven't given it any consideration, but... Hmm, could I ask you a question?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ask away.

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: The famous adventurer Stanley of Mondstadt is so famed because he passed through the Mare Jivari, but he lost a dear friend during that adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: Even though few people know what the name of that friend was, the memory of him stays with us adventurers because he went on that adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Zhiqiong
dialogues.text: I was thinking... and please, don't laugh if you find me immature. Do you think that this friend of Stanley's, who did not return, has not in fact passed on, but instead can be said to be truly "alive"?

choices.text: The only thing that matters is life itself.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: But to be remembered... Even if you were to pass on early, would that not be considered an extension of your life?

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: You would live on in a different fashion, in the admiration, memories... in the eyes of others.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't be so concerned about what other people think.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: That's what a lot of people have told me. "Be yourself," "just do your job"... These things sound like guidance, but really, they're asking me to give up.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: I've said before, I think, but I don't go on adventures for anyone else... or for myself, even.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: Hmm, have you thought about this before?

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: This world has been ordered by the gods, and though we ordinary mortals have not been given "eyes" by them, we nonetheless do not wish to go quietly and be forgotten just like that.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: I believe that this discontent is not meaningless, and that's why I go around exploring dangerous areas. I mean...

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: I mean, to wrestle with things that even the gods would fear with our frail forms... isn't that what makes us "human"? That's what I believe.

choices.text: Still, you're not the only person who has the right to bestow meaning upon an adventure.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: I know... I won't forget the help everyone gave me... and I won't forget the trouble I caused you, either. This adventure, after all, wasn't undertaken by me alone.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: Isn't that what adventurers are?

choices.text: Back to playing the hero now, are we?

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: Heh, I'm still a long way off from where you are... Rather than a "hero," I'd call myself someone who "isn't afraid of dying so that they might truly live."

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: This was something that a senior from Sumeru told me, and she herself heard it from the Eremites.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: That makes sense...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon thinks you're more like "someone who keeps chasing after misfortune"!

choices.text: I suppose being remembered is also a form of success.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: Well... I've never thought of living a "successful" life. Rather, even if I "fail," I would like to leave an impression on others.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: At least they would say, "Zhiqiong also did once face the challenges of The Chasm!"

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: At least then, I wouldn't be forgotten like those who sacrificed themselves in deserted places, or... you know, like me now.

choices.text: I've never thought about this issue.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: Is that so...? I guess that might be because an outsider like you naturally becomes the topic of conversation no matter where you go.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: I suppose it's like how children born with golden spoons in their mouths might find the idea of poverty to be an exciting, but ultimately unnecessary, avenue for adventure.

response.speaker: Zhiqiong
response.text: Ah, uh, sorry... I didn't mean it like that. I was just saying... Never mind. Just forget I said anything.
